name: Purple Grenadier
rangeDescription: Southeastern south sudan, southern ethiopia, somalia, northeastern uganda, kenya, and tanzania
description: A distinctive and attractive waxbill with a deep-blue tail and a red bill. Males are more colorful, with a purple belly, a rufous hood, and purple and red around the eye.

name: Northern Chestnut-breasted Wren
rangeDescription: Central and western andes of colombia to peru (san martín)
description: Found at higher elevations than other members of its genus. Shy and uncommon denizen of forest undergrowth from 1,100–2,000 m.

name: Sulawesi Scops-Owl
rangeDescription: Sulawesi
description: A small brown owl with yellow eyes and feathered ear tufts. Note square head shape when tufts not raised.

name: Bioko Batis
rangeDescription: Bioko (gulf of guinea)
description: The only batis on Bioko. Patterned like a typical batis, with a white belly and throat, black wings with a white bar, and a black face.

name: White-bellied Imperial-Pigeon
rangeDescription: Mountains of sulawesi and sula islands (taliabu and mangole)
description: A distinctive large, spectacularly-marked pigeon. Green with a conspicuous pale gray head, a red eye-ring around a beady yellow eye, a dark neck and chest, a bold white belly, a chestnut base to the undertail, and a broad white band in the otherwise dark tail.

name: Taiwan Liocichla
rangeDescription: Montane forest of taiwan
description: The gloom of the forest may make this small songbird of dense montane forests and edges appear dark, but a bit of sunlight reveals a gloriously colorful plumage, with subtle patches of olive, blue, yellow, orange, and chestnut. Social, moving about in pairs or flocks, often emerging out into the open when gaps in the vegetation are present.

name: Colima Warbler
rangeDescription: Western texas (chisos mountains) to central mexico
description: Rather drab warbler of highlands in Mexico. Dusky gray-brown overall with grayer head, bold white eyering, buffy flanks, and mustard-yellow undertail coverts.

name: Eastern Marsh Harrier
rangeDescription: Eastern asia; winters to southeastern asia, philippines, and indonesia
description: A common patroller above reedbeds, flying with wings raised in a shallow V-shape. Adult males are predominantly pale gray with a dark-speckled head, blackish back with pale-edged feathers, and black wingtips.

name: Rufous Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Arid coastal northwestern peru (tumbes to northern lima)
description: Large flycatcher restricted to dry lowland forest in northwestern Peru, especially in areas with abundant mesquite and acacia. Well named; no other flycatcher in range is similarly colored.

name: Small Blue Kingfisher
rangeDescription: Southern sumatra, java, bali, lombok, sumbawa, and kangean islands
description: Tiny sky-blue kingfisher with a snowy-white throat, belly, and facial patches. Male averages bluer than female, which has a greenish cast.

name: Rufous-crowned Prinia
rangeDescription: Northeastern india (assam) to bangladesh, western myanmar, and southern china
description: Very long-tailed prinia of hilly and montane areas, descending to foothills in winter. Note rufous crown, warm brown upperparts and sides, and gray cheeks and pale belly.

name: Bannerman's Sunbird
rangeDescription: Northern angola to southeastern democratic republic of the congo and far northwestern zambia
description: A medium-sized sunbird with an olive back and gray belly. Male has a metallic bluish (may appear green in some light) hood and breast; female appears plain-headed with limited metallic plumage on crown.

name: Brazilian Tinamou
rangeDescription: Tropical southern amazonian brazil, adjacent eastern peru and northwestern bolivia
description: Dark, subtly-patterned tinamou. Cold grayish brown, with a more reddish head and variable black barring on the wings; females are more strongly barred than males.

name: Lynes's Cisticola
rangeDescription: Highlands of eastern uganda and central kenya
description: Medium-sized, streak-backed cisticola of middle-elevation uplands. Found in grassland and savanna on rocky slopes with a mix of bushes, grass, and often aloes.

name: Cinnamon-tailed Fantail
rangeDescription: Tanimbar islands (larat, yamdena, lutu, mutu, and selaru) and babar
description: A distinctive songbird with a long tail, often cocked to expose the diagnostic cinnamon sides. Also note the gray back, cinnamon flash in the wing, and buff belly.

name: Black-hooded Sunbeam
rangeDescription: Andes of western bolivia (la paz and cochabamba)
description: Unique and spectacular hummingbird of the upper humid montane forest in Bolivia. Plumage mostly black, with striking white feathers on breast and a shining blue rump.

name: Crested Hornero
rangeDescription: Chaco of southeastern bolivia to western paraguay and northern argentina
description: A mostly terrestrial and chunky light brown bird of the north and central Chaco, from central Argentina to Western Paraguay and extreme SE Bolivia. Distinguished from Rufous Hornero by crest, from Lark-like Brushrunner by plain plumage, and from Cachalotes by dull plumage, smaller bill and size, and dark iris.

name: Blue-capped Puffleg
rangeDescription: Andes of southern bolivia and northwestern argentina
description: Generally rare (but locally fairly common in a few spots) hummingbird of humid forests just below treeline on the eastern slope of the Andes from NW Argentina to La Paz, Bolivia. Often feeds near treefalls and roadcuts, especially on bellflowers (Lobelioideae).

name: Chestnut-breasted Quail-thrush
rangeDescription: South-central queensland and adjacent northwestern new south wales
description: Heavily patterned terrestrial bird of western Queensland and northwestern New South Wales. Both sexes have pale eyebrow, gray-brown back, speckled undertail, and black-and-white markings on wing.

name: Henderson Petrel
rangeDescription: Breeds henderson island (southeastern pacific); wintering range unknown
description: A typical uniformly grayish-brown petrel with pale mottling at the base of the bill that gives it a somewhat “frosted” facial appearance. Pale bar along the leading edge of the underwing between the body and elbow is evident in flight.
